subject: [bugfix][NPU] Fix startup bug in olmoe 1b 7b (#31782)
pr_body:
## Motivation



Serving `OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct` on Ascend NPU crashes on the first forward pass:

```
File ".../srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py", line 88, in _init_routing
    active_num=num_tokens * top_k,
TypeError: unsupported operand type(s) for *: 'int' and 'NoneType'
```

`top_k` reaches `npu_moe_init_routing_v2` as `None`.

**Root cause:** The NPU MoE refactor (#25663) moved `top_k` from being derived at runtime — the old `fused_moe_method_npu.py` always took `top_k = topk_ids.shape[1]` / `topk_weights.shape[-1]` inside forward — to being read once at construction time from `moe_runner_config.top_k` (cached as `AscendTPDispatcher.top_k`). Models that do not pass `top_k` into `FusedMoE` (e.g. `olmoe.py`, currently the only MoE model in-tree that omits it) leave `moe_runner_config.top_k = None`, and that `None` propagates through `AscendTPDispatcher.top_k` into `_init_routing`, blowing up at `num_tokens * top_k`.


## Modifications



- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/ascend_tp.py`: In `AscendTPDispatcher.dispatch()`, re-derive `self.top_k` from the actual topk output shape (`self.top_k = topk_weights.shape[-1]`) right before invoking `self.init._init_routing`.

This restores the pre-refactor protection where the routing kernel always used the runtime topk width, making the dispatcher robust to a `None` config `top_k` regardless of whether the model layer supplied it to `FusedMoE`. Single-file, minimal, no new compute (the topk tensor is already materialized in `dispatch()`).

## Accuracy Tests



NA

## Speed Tests and Profiling



N/A — correctness fix only. The change reassigns a scalar from a tensor shape that is already materialized in `dispatch()`; no new kernel calls or compute are introduced.

subject: [Bugfix][Kernel] Correct FlashInfer CUTLASS MoE tuning token bound (#46838)
pr_body:
## Purpose

Previously, #34542 refactored the FlashInfer CUTLASS fused MoE backend and passed the CUDA graph max capture size (typically 512) as `tune_max_num_tokens` for flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe. However, `max_capture_size` describes graph capture capacity and can be unrelated to the scheduler/MoE max batched token limit, so using it can select a tuning configuration for the wrong token range and thus cause suboptimal perf unexpectedly.

This PR partially reverts #34542 and leaves `tune_max_num_tokens` as the default value (8192 defined in FlashInfer). Conceptually, the best value for `tune_max_num_tokens` is `FusedMoEConfig.max_num_tokens * parallel_factor`, but the parallel factor can vary across different parallel configurations and erroneous to determine (as pointed out in [this comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46838#issuecomment-4834365663)), so we currently leave it as default, which is the behavior before #34542.

### Related Issue

This is part of the effort for #41306 to fix FlashInfer Cutlass fused MoE perf regression. There are also ongoing FlashInfer side fixes and optimizations to improve the MoE perf.

## Test Plan

#### Functional

```

```

subject: [Bugfix] Size FlashInfer NVLink MNNVL workspace to EP group (#40893)
pr_body:
## Summary
Fix `FlashInferNVLinkOneSidedManager` and `FlashInferNVLinkTwoSidedManager` so the MNNVL workspace is sized to the EP group instead of the DP group.

In both managers, the flashinfer-allocated workspace tensor's leading dimension is determined by the comm_backend's group size (via `MnnvlMemory.set_comm_from_config` -> `comm_backend.Split(...)` -> `Get_size`; vLLM's `CustomCommunicator.Split` is a no-op that returns `self`), while the kernel-side dimension comes from the manager's view of the EP group:

- One-sided (`MoeAlltoAll` + `moe_a2a_get_workspace_size_per_rank`): kernel asserts `workspace.size(0) == moe_ep_size`, where `moe_ep_size = self.world_size`.
- Two-sided (`MnnvlMoe.get_moe_workspaces`): workspace stride is sized to `mapping.tp_size`, which is set to `self.world_size` in this manager.

Both paths previously wired `CustomCommunicator(get_dp_group().cpu_group)`, sizing the workspace to the DP group. Whenever `dp_size != ep_size` -- i.e. the standard TP>1 + DP>1 EP configuration -- the two dimensions disagree (the one-sided kernel asserts on first dispatch; the two-sided allocation is similarly mismatched, presumably hidden today because typical two-sided users run TP=1, where DP == EP).

These managers only ever live on the EP `CudaCommunicator` (gated on `is_ep_communicator and data_parallel_size > 1` in [`base_device_communicator.py`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/main/vllm/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py)), so `self.cpu_group` is the EP group by construction (size = `DP * PCP * TP`) and matches the kernels' expectation for any combination of DP / PCP / TP.

## Why this is not a duplicate
Searched open PRs on `vllm-project/vllm` for `FlashInferNVLinkOneSided`, `flashinfer_nvlink_one_sided`, `MnnvlConfig`, and `all2all.py + MnnvlConfig` -- no open PR addresses this bug.

## Test plan
Reproduced and verified end-to-end with the configuration that originally hit the assertion (TP=2, DP=4, EP, hybrid LB on Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4):

```bash
vllm serve nvidia/Kimi-K2.5-NVFP4 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --language-model-only \
    --load-format fastsafetensors \
    -tp 2 \
    -dp  …[truncated]

subject: [ROCm][CI] Fix AITER test flakiness by using explicit attention backend (#32346)
pr_body:
## Summary

This PR fixes test failures for `TitanML/tiny-mixtral` when running AITER tests on ROCm as part of the full test suite.

## Problem

When running the test suite as a group, the following tests were failing:
- `test_models[True-True-5-32-TitanML/tiny-mixtral]`
- `test_models[False-True-5-32-TitanML/tiny-mixtral]`

**Notably, these tests pass when run individually.** The failures only occur when running multiple tests together, showing logprobs mismatches between HuggingFace and vLLM outputs with top token rankings differing slightly (e.g., 'fact' vs 'upset' with ~0.3 logprob difference).

## Investigation

Several potential causes of state leakage between tests were investigated:

1. **MoE config LRU cache** (`get_moe_configs` in `fused_moe.py`) - Cleared via `cache_clear()`, but cache showed 0 hits/misses for Mixtral, ruling this out
2. **torch.compile/Dynamo cache** - Attempted reset via `torch._dynamo.reset()`
3. **GPU memory state** - Added `torch.cuda.synchronize()` and `torch.cuda.empty_cache()`

These mitigations did not resolve the issue. The previous implementation used `monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", "1")` which enables the **full AITER stack**. We suspect the full AITER stack introduces state or kernel selection decisions that persist across tests in ways that are difficult to fully reset, causing numerical divergence.

## Solution

Replace the environment variable approach with explicit `attention_backend="ROCM_AITER_FA"` parameter. This:
- Tests the AITER **attention backend** specifically (which is the intended test target)
- Eliminates the state leakage issue by not activating the problematic code paths

## Changes

- Removed `monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER", "1")` 
- Added `attention_backend="ROCM_AITER_FA"` via `rocm_kwargs` when `use_rocm_aiter=True`

## Testing

Verified all tests pass when running the full test suite:
```bash
pytest -v -s tests/models/language -m 'core_model and (not slow_test)'
```

subject: [AMD][Quantization][Bugfix] Fix bug related to fp8 max on gfx95x for per-token-group quant (ROCm) (#30900)
pr_body:
## Motivation

`_per_token_group_quant_8bit_raw` in `fp8_kernel.py` hardcodes the fp8 clamp/scale bound to `224.0` for all ROCm devices, but the fp8 range is device-dependent: `e4m3fnuz` (max 224.0) on gfx94x (MI300) vs `e4m3fn` (max 448.0) on gfx95x (MI355X). The module already resolves this correctly as `fp8_max`, but this function ignores it.

On gfx95x this computes the per-group scale as `absmax / 224` instead of `absmax / 448`. It round-trips (no crash/NaN), but only the `[-224, 224]` subset of the `±448` `e4m3fn` range is used — wasting ~1 bit of precision and causing silent accuracy degradation on MI355X. gfx94x and CUDA are unaffected.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8_kernel.py`: in the ROCm fp8 branch of `_per_token_group_quant_8bit_raw`, use the device-resolved `fp8_max` instead of the hardcoded `224.0`. One-line functional change; the `int8` branch (and its pre-existing `# TODO incorrect for int8`) is left unchanged.
- `test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_fp8_kernel_hip_max.py` (new): runs the **real** Triton quant kernel (no mocking) on gfx950, feeds a group whose absmax equals the `e4m3fn` max (448.0), and asserts the emitted per-group scale is `1.0` (= `448/448`). On the unfixed code the scale is `448/224 = 2.0`, so the test fails. Gated to gfx95x (`is_hip() and is_gfx95_supported()`) and registered to the MI355X CI suite `stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`.

## Test

Verified on real MI355X (gfx950) hardware — the new test fails on the current `224.0` and passes with the fix:

```
# reverted to 224.0
FAILED test/.../test_fp8_kernel_hip_max.py::...::test_hip_fp8_scale_uses_e4m3fn_max_448
# with fp8_max fix
1 passed
```

subject: [AMD][Fix] Qwen3.5: guard zero-grid launch in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm(_with_gate) (HIP invalid configuration on idle DP rank) (#31794)
pr_body:
## Motivation

Bringing up **Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8** with MoRI expert-parallel all-to-all (`--moe-a2a-backend mori`) and `--enable-dp-attention` on MI355X/ROCm surfaces three connected failures. This PR fixes the two that live in the model / idle-rank path (bug #2 and bug #3 below); bug #1 is the prerequisite init fix already handled in #31793.

**Bug #1 — Qwen shared-expert fusion vs. per-rank EP layout (prerequisite, fixed in #31793).** Qwen uses a single global shared-expert slot with a per-token gate, while MoRI / DeepEP-family backends use per-rank expert slots. The mismatch trips a model-init assertion / mis-maps the shared-expert id. #31793 disables the global-slot shared-expert fusion under per-rank EP backends. It must be applied for the model to load past init.

**Bug #2 — idle DP-attention ranks launch zero-sized grids (fixes #31350, #31594).** Under DP attention an active rank may hold e.g. 80 tokens while the other DP ranks hold 0. Many Triton/AITER kernels grid on the token count, so an empty rank launches with grid `(0, ...)`. CUDA tolerates a zero-sized grid as a no-op; **HIP rejects it with `invalid configuration argument`** (surfacing asynchronously later, e.g. during decode CUDA-graph capture / the Mamba allocator).

```
File ".../srt/models/utils.py", in fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_with_gate
    _fused_qk_gemma_rmsnorm_gate_kernel[(q_rows,)](...)   # grid == (0,)
torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: invalid configuration argument
```

**Bug #3 — MoRI was misrouted through the plain TP-MoE path (root-cause collective fix).** `Qwen2MoeSparseMoeBlock` only took the EP dispatch/combine path for `get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()`. MoRI uses EP dispatch/combine but is not `.is_deepep()`, so it fell into the ordinary TP path and ran a `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce()` **after** combine. Combine already returns each token to its source rank, so the trailing all-reduce mixed mismatched per-rank shapes — active rank `[80, 4096]` vs. idle rank `[0, 4096]` — a heterogeneous collective that crashes or deadlocks custom all-reduce.

## Modifications
